extracted.intended_audience: K23 career development applicants, mentors, and NIH grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review summary (NIH NIAID MID-B) for a K23 Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award resubmission, evaluating the candidate, training plan, research plan, mentors, environment, human/animal subject protections, and related compliance/resource-sharing items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: summarizes the final opinion of the committee after discussion and is the basis for the assigned Overall Impact/Priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by individual reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting nor calculated into the overall impact score. The Resume and Summary of Discussion section summarizes the final opinion of the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess candidate qualifications, prior training, publications, awards, references, and potential to become an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: well-trained physician, varied training (residency, Peds ID fellowship), international clinical training, postdoctoral fellowship, multiple awards, improved publication record (3 first-author in past 3 years / total 6 with 4 first-author), current PI on two grants, strong reference letters. Weaknesses: none were noted by reviewers in this resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate clarity and appropriateness of career development plan, defined short- and long-term goals, mentoring structure, and didactic/training activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: 5 defined short-term, obtainable goals; regular mentoring meetings (weekly/biweekly/quarterly advisory committee); coursework (formal courses with credits); plan complements research and includes MS in Clinical Research; training in international project management, computational biology, machine learning, biostatistics, grant writing, leadership. Weaknesses: none noted. Reviewers look for non-duplicative coursework and integration with project and mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate significance, innovation, hypotheses/aims, experimental design, methods, preliminary data, power/sample size, rigor, anticipated pitfalls and alternatives, and feasibility relative to candidate goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: significant topic (malaria vaccine development), use of field-derived human samples and mosquito data, unique peptide microarray (up to 392,000 peptides / >170,000 described), meaningful aims (Aim 1 identify serologic correlates of protection; Aim 2 in silico epitope prediction and functional testing), appropriate machine learning (Random Forest) with training/testing replication, power analysis included, added in vitro liver model and functional assays. Weaknesses: concerns about predictive accuracy of in silico/antibody epitope models (antibody epitope prediction less ideal than T-cell), whether protection is solely antibody-mediated (cell-mediated immunity not addressed), unclear contribution of mosquito experiments to parasite genetic diversity characterization, reproducibility/adequacy of matching mosquitoes to bloodmeal source (25/28 matched; was done once). Reviewers assess whether aims are appropriately designed to train the candidate and support future R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess expertise, availability, evidence of active mentoring, appropriateness of mentoring letters, and how mentors address the candidate's needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: well-qualified mentoring team covering international research design, molecular epidemiology, data science, peptide microarrays, vaccinology, and in vitro models; addition of immunologist John Adams with hands-on training (two months in his lab); detailed mentoring letters specifying meeting cadence; advisory committee with relevant experts; prior productive collaborations (coauthored papers). Weaknesses: none noted. Reviewers expect explicit mentoring plans, frequency of interactions, and commitment to candidate development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate institutional resources, facilities, support, and protected time commitment for the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: outstanding environment at University of Maryland (Center for Vaccine Development and Global Health), documented Malawi site facilities (University of Malawi College of Medicine, Malaria Alert Center), Adams lab facilities for training, institutional letter committing at least 75% protected research time and intent to appoint candidate to faculty. Weaknesses: none noted. Reviewers look for evidence that the environment will enhance candidate progress and provide necessary equipment/space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess protections for human subjects and adequacy of plans for human subject research (risk mitigation, consent, confidentiality, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code 30 ACCEPTABLE. This study involves characterization of humoral responses before and after exposure to infectious mosquito bites using samples collected as part of a Malawi ICEMR cohort. Reviewers noted precautions taken when handling human blood/specimens and availability of adequate biohazard equipment. 'Human Subjects: 30 - Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns' is recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the plan for inclusion of women is appropriate and acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code G1A ACCEPTABLE. The study will recruit participants without regard to [sex]; reviewers marked inclusion plan acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess plans for inclusion of minority participants and whether the study population is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code M5A ACCEPTABLE. All participants will be Malawians of African descent; plan judged acceptable by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Individuals Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess inclusion across age ranges and whether age-related plans are scientifically acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code C2A ACCEPTABLE. Samples for Aim 1 will be serum from children aged 6 months to 15 years; reviewers found inclusion across the lifespan acceptable for the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate use of vertebrate animals, appropriateness of species/age/number, and animal welfare protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code 30 ACCEPTABLE. Female and male New Zealand white rabbits aged <1 year will be used for generation of antibodies; reviewers noted no SRG concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess biosafety precautions, handling of infectious materials, and availability of appropriate biosafety equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACCEPTABLE. Revised application addresses precautions for human blood and specimens; adequate biohazard equipment is available at research locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether candidate has appropriate RCR training planned or completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACCEPTABLE. Candidate has taken several RCR and human subjects training courses and will take an additional 1-credit RCR course; resubmission included more detailed description of training taken and planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate applicability of select agent regulations to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOT APPLICABLE as noted in the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess adequacy of plans for sharing data, model organisms, genomic data, and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RESOURCE SHARING PLANS: ACCEPTABLE. Headings for Data Sharing Plan, Model Organisms Sharing Plan, and Genomic Data Sharing Plan are included; reviewers marked resource sharing acceptable. Specific plan text is recorded in application (not fully reproduced here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess justification for foreign site involvement and acceptability of foreign institution arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOREIGN INSTITUTION: JUSTIFIED. Human and entomological samples will be collected as part of the Malawi ICEMR cohort that began in 2019; reviewers accepted foreign institution justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plans for authentication of reagents, cell lines, and other critical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACCEPTABLE. The revised authentication of reagents is described as acceptable and very detailed in the resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee guidance regarding recommended budget adjustments or allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACCEPTABLE. The budget is recommended as requested in all years; administrative note that final costs will be calculated by institute grants management staff based on committee recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Responsiveness / Revision Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a resubmitted (amended) application adequately addresses prior critiques and improves on weaknesses from the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions: Comments or Concerns: Acceptable. Multiple reviewers explicitly noted the resubmission addressed prior critiques (added immunology mentor, in vitro model training, machine learning details, more documentation of Malawi site, additional preliminary data and authentication) and judged the application much improved or outstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Process and Criterion Scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural description of how criterion and overall scores are submitted and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking.' Reviewers' criterion-specific comments (strengths/weaknesses) accompany the summary but do not directly map to the overall numeric score calculation at the meeting.
